did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ahab told Jezebel not only about Elijah’s deeds, but also about the killing of the prophets by the sword.
Did you know? Jezebel threatened Elijah with a solemn oath, saying that by the next day she would kill him just as the prophets had been killed.
Did you know? Elijah came to Beersheba in Judah, left his servant there, and went on alone for a full day into the wilderness, where he asked to die.
Did you know? When Elijah awoke, he found a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water by his head. After eating and drinking, he went back to sleep.
Did you know? Elijah ate and drank a second time, and strengthened by that food, he traveled for forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
Did you know? At Horeb, a powerful wind, an earthquake, and a fire passed before Elijah, but the text emphasizes that the Lord was not in them. Afterward came a gentle whisper.
Did you know? When Elijah heard the gentle whisper, he covered his face with his cloak and stood at the entrance of the cave.
Did you know? After the revelation at Horeb, Elijah was commanded to return on his way and carry out tasks involving Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha.
Did you know? Despite Elijah’s feeling of loneliness, the Lord told him that seven thousand people remained in Israel who had not bowed down to Baal or kissed him.
Did you know? Elisha was plowing with twelve pairs of oxen. Elijah threw his cloak over him, signaling his call to become a prophet.
